newsitem.title: UK: Shepherd Neame annual pre-tax profits up five pct.
newsitem.headline: Shepherd Neame annual pre-tax profits up five pct.

text.p: Shepherd Neame Ltd, Britain's oldest brewery, said on Thursday that annual pre-tax profits rose to 5.8 million stg from 5.5 million, marking 21 successive years of profit growth.

However, Shepherd Neame, which has its shares listed on London's Ofex market, said that the differential of excise duty between the UK and France was continuing to have a marked negative effect on the public house and trade business, as the UK's high excise duties prompt alcohol shoppers to visit France.
Shepherd Neame said imports acccount for around four percent of total UK beer sales and 15 pct of all take home sales.
"The freedom with which hundreds of vans full of beer and tobacco come into Dover every day amounts to a smugglers charter," said Shepherd Neame in a statement.

Shepherd Neame raised its dividend payment by six percent to 20.5p and saw earnings per share increase to 66p in the year to June 30, 1996 from 62.9p in 1995. Turnover increased seven percent to 51.5 million stg.
